mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.5% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the past two months indicates a strengthening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of broader economic growth and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where HOUST increased by more than 5% in the prior two months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points over the last month suggests a tightening labor market, which typically leads to wage inflation and increased consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where UNRATE decreased by more than 0.3pp in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the last month signals increased economic activity, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO increased by more than 1% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over the past three months indicates strong consumer demand, which is a key driver of economic growth and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the periods with sustained RSAFS growth.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure and tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2 percentage points in the same month, it indicates a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200k and UNRATE decrease > 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the GDP (GDPC1) by more than 0.5% over the last quarter signals a weakening economy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where GDPC1 decreased by more than 0.5% in the prior quarter.
